Using tradeR

Source: vignettes/articles/guide.Rmd
guide.Rmd

This section of the site is the guide to every public class and member of the tradeR package, laid out like Zerodha’s Kite Connect documentation: each guide page opens with a summary table, then gives each member its own section with its arguments, an example, what it returns and what it signals. This page is the index of all of them, one table per page, so you can find any member in one scroll. The reference section holds the roxygen2 documentation of every class, generated from the package source.

The package is an R face on the Unified Broker Interface (UBI), a REST API that combines ten Indian stock brokers into one account. It is a native R port of the Python library tradingmachine, with the same classes, members and argument names, so code moves between the two by writing $ where Python writes .. Almost every member here sends one request to UBI, and each member’s section names the UBI route it calls.

How to read the kinds

Every member in the tables below has a kind, which says what sort of thing it is. The kind matters most for “places orders”, because those members send real orders to real brokers. The table below explains each kind.

Kind Meaning
active binding Reads a value from UBI each time you access it, and never writes anything. It is written without brackets: instrument$last_price. Assigning to it signals an error.
method Takes arguments and reads only. It is written with brackets: instrument$prices(days = 10).
generator function Called on the class generator rather than on an instrument, to find instruments: Equity$search("nse", "RELI"). It stands in for a Python class method.
places orders Sends orders to a broker, or cancels or changes them. These act on real money.
class An R6 class you construct with $new().

The rule behind the first two kinds is the package’s own, inherited from the Python library: anything that only reports a value is an active binding, and only members that take an argument or write to the market are methods.

Instruments 3

Three pages hold classes rather than members. Synthetic orders documents the synthetic order classes in the R/orders_*.R files, one for each type UBI’s order engine runs, Instruments documents the 27 instrument classes, and Asset baskets documents the five kinds of basket in the R/asset_baskets_*.R files and the classes that store them. The fourteen classes of candle analysis, 209 methods from indicators to the performance measures, have their own Analysis section, and every instrument and every basket inherits them.

Instruments

An instrument is looked up once when you construct it, and from then on every member reads from UBI. The Instruments page documents the 27 classes, such as Equity$new("nse", "RELIANCE") or EquityIndexOption$new("nse", "NIFTY", "2026-09-29", 25000, "CE"), and the fields the lookup fills in. The first two members below belong to every instrument class, and the third only to indices and funds. set_shared_unified_broker_interface() has no Python counterpart; it was added in the R port so that a script or a test can install a client of its own, such as one built with credentials.

Kind Member Description
generator function Instrument$shared_unified_broker_interface() Returns the one client all instruments share, creating it on first use.
generator function Instrument$set_shared_unified_broker_interface() Installs a client of your choosing as the one all instruments share.
active binding constituents The stored basket of what an index, an exchange traded fund or a mutual fund holds, on the four index classes, ExchangeTradedFund and MutualFund.

Market data

These members read candles, quotes and the order book. The first four work on every instrument; the order-book values exist only on instruments that can be traded, because an index has no order book.

Kind Member Description
method prices() Fetches the instrument’s candles for a range from UBI.
active binding quote The instrument’s full unified quote, read from UBI on every access.
active binding last_price The instrument’s last traded price, read from UBI on every access.
active binding ohlc The day’s open, high and low with the last and previous close prices, read from UBI on every access.
active binding bids The buy side of the order book, read from UBI on every access.
active binding offers The sell side of the order book, read from UBI on every access.
active binding best_bid The highest bid in the order book.
active binding best_offer The lowest offer in the order book.
active binding bid_offer_spread The gap between the best offer and the best bid, measured from one quote.
active binding mid_price The price halfway between the best bid and the best offer, from one quote.
active binding volume_weighted_average_price Today’s volume weighted average price.
active binding last_quantity The quantity of the last trade.
active binding total_traded_volume The quantity traded so far today.
active binding open_interest The open interest of a future or an option.
active binding last_trade_time When the last trade happened.

Finding instruments

These generator functions find instruments rather than read one. search() exists on the cash and index classes, and the other four exist on every derivative class’s generator, each of which names its own segment. In Python they are defined once on the Futures and Option base classes and inherited; R6 generators do not inherit functions, so the R port writes them out on each class, and Futures$expiries() and the other functions on the base classes only signal an error, as calling them on the Python base classes does.

Kind Member Description
generator function search() Finds listed instruments whose symbol contains a term, on the cash and index classes.
generator function expiries() Lists the expiry dates a derivative is listed for.
generator function contracts() Lists the contracts on an underlying as a data frame of identities.
generator function strikes() Lists the strike prices listed on one underlying for one expiry.
generator function chain() Lists every option listed on one underlying for one expiry.

Derivatives

These members report what a futures or option contract has and a share does not: its expiry, its underlying, its basis, and for an option its moneyness, implied volatility and greeks. They are defined on the derivative base classes and inherited by all sixteen futures and option classes, and none of them places an order. Those marked futures or options exist only on that kind of contract.

Kind Member Description
active binding days_to_expiry The calendar days left until the contract expires.
active binding expired Whether the expiry date has passed.
active binding expiry_kind Whether the contract is the month’s last expiry or a weekly one.
active binding next_expiry The next expiry after this one, where a position rolls to.
active binding underlying The underlying instrument, built afresh on every read.
active binding underlying_price The underlying’s last traded price.
active binding open_interest_day_high The highest open interest reached today.
active binding open_interest_day_low The lowest open interest reached today.
active binding contract_value What one lot is worth at the last price.
active binding basis How far a future’s price is above its underlying’s. Futures only.
active binding basis_percent The basis as a percentage of the underlying’s price. Futures only.
active binding cost_of_carry The basis as a yearly rate. Futures only.
active binding is_call, is_put Whether an option is a call or a put. Options only.
active binding intrinsic_value What the option would be worth if exercised now. Options only.
active binding time_value The part of the premium above the intrinsic value. Options only.
active binding in_the_money Whether the option has intrinsic value. Options only.
active binding moneyness_percent How far in or out of the money the option is, in per cent. Options only.
active binding breakeven_price The underlying price at which a buyer breaks even at expiry. Options only.
active binding premium_per_lot What one lot costs to buy. Options only.
active binding notional_value What one lot controls at the strike price. Options only.
method implied_volatility() The volatility the option’s price implies. Options only.
method greeks() The option’s fair price, delta, gamma, theta, vega and rho. Options only.

Orders

The members that place orders send real orders.

Members of the kind “places orders” send orders through UBI to real brokers, with real money. Pass dry_run = TRUE to place_order(), modify_order() or cancel_order() to have UBI check an order and show the request it would send, without sending it.

These members place, change and cancel orders in one instrument, read that instrument’s rows out of the day’s order book and trade book, and read the order engine’s parents, which are the synthetic orders and held limit orders UBI is working.

Kind Member Description
places orders place_order() Places one order in this instrument through UBI.
places orders modify_order() Changes one pending order through UBI.
places orders cancel_order() Cancels one pending order through UBI.
places orders cancel_open_orders() Cancels every order in this instrument that is still waiting, whether at a broker or held in UBI’s order engine.
places orders cancel_parent() Cancels one of the order engine’s parents, with every leg it still has resting at a broker, or one part of a plan.
active binding orders Every one of today’s orders in this instrument, whatever its status.
active binding open_orders Today’s orders in this instrument that can still be changed.
active binding completed_orders Today’s orders in this instrument that filled in full.
active binding rejected_orders Today’s orders in this instrument that a broker or the exchange refused.
active binding cancelled_orders Today’s orders in this instrument that were cancelled.
active binding trades Today’s trades in this instrument.
active binding parents This instrument’s synthetic orders and held orders that the order engine has not finished.
method parent() Reads one of the order engine’s parents, whether or not it has finished.
method parent_orders() Today’s broker orders that one parent placed.
method parent_trades() Today’s trades in the broker orders that one parent placed.

Price wrappers

Each wrapper is place_order() with the price source written into its name, so buy_at_best_bid_price(quantity = 1, product = "cnc") joins the queue at the best bid. Apart from the market and limit pairs, UBI works out the price itself when it sends the order. The sixteen wrappers below name a single price.

Kind Member Description
places orders buy_at_market_price() Buys at whatever price the market is asking.
places orders sell_at_market_price() Sells at whatever price the market is bidding.
places orders buy_at_limit_price() Buys at a price of your choosing, or better.
places orders sell_at_limit_price() Sells at a price of your choosing, or better.
places orders buy_at_best_bid_price() Buys patiently, joining the queue at the highest price anyone is bidding.
places orders buy_at_best_offer_price() Buys at once, by crossing the spread to the lowest price anyone is offering.
places orders sell_at_best_offer_price() Sells patiently, joining the queue at the lowest price anyone is offering.
places orders sell_at_best_bid_price() Sells at once, by crossing the spread to the highest price anyone is bidding.
places orders buy_at_mid_price() Buys halfway between the best bid and the best offer.
places orders sell_at_mid_price() Sells halfway between the best bid and the best offer.
places orders buy_at_volume_weighted_average_price() Buys at the average price the day has traded at so far.
places orders sell_at_volume_weighted_average_price() Sells at the average price the day has traded at so far.
places orders buy_at_marketable_price() Buys now with a limit order priced at the best offer, the price it takes to fill immediately.
places orders sell_at_marketable_price() Sells now with a limit order priced at the best bid, the price it takes to fill immediately.
places orders buy_at_last_price() Buys with a limit order at the price the instrument last traded at.
places orders sell_at_last_price() Sells with a limit order at the price the instrument last traded at.

The other sixteen reach deeper into the order book, from the second to the fifth price on each side. They are listed in the collapsed table below, which opens when you click its title.

The sixteen depth-level wrappers
Kind Member Description
places orders buy_at_second_best_bid_price() Buys at the second best price on the buy side of the book.
places orders buy_at_third_best_bid_price() Buys at the third best price on the buy side of the book.
places orders buy_at_fourth_best_bid_price() Buys at the fourth best price on the buy side of the book.
places orders buy_at_fifth_best_bid_price() Buys at the fifth best price on the buy side of the book.
places orders sell_at_second_best_bid_price() Sells at the second best price on the buy side of the book.
places orders sell_at_third_best_bid_price() Sells at the third best price on the buy side of the book.
places orders sell_at_fourth_best_bid_price() Sells at the fourth best price on the buy side of the book.
places orders sell_at_fifth_best_bid_price() Sells at the fifth best price on the buy side of the book.
places orders buy_at_second_best_offer_price() Buys at the second best price on the sell side of the book.
places orders buy_at_third_best_offer_price() Buys at the third best price on the sell side of the book.
places orders buy_at_fourth_best_offer_price() Buys at the fourth best price on the sell side of the book.
places orders buy_at_fifth_best_offer_price() Buys at the fifth best price on the sell side of the book.
places orders sell_at_second_best_offer_price() Sells at the second best price on the sell side of the book.
places orders sell_at_third_best_offer_price() Sells at the third best price on the sell side of the book.
places orders sell_at_fourth_best_offer_price() Sells at the fourth best price on the sell side of the book.
places orders sell_at_fifth_best_offer_price() Sells at the fifth best price on the sell side of the book.

Positions

These members act on this instrument’s positions without being told which side you are on, so a long position is reduced by selling and a short one by buying.

Kind Member Description
active binding net_positions The positions held in this instrument now, merged across every broker.
active binding day_positions Today’s own positions in this instrument, without what was carried in.
active binding positions_value What this instrument’s open positions are worth at the moment.
active binding positions_pnl What this instrument’s positions have made or lost.
places orders add_to_position() Makes an existing position bigger, or opens a new one.
places orders reduce_position() Makes an existing position smaller, without turning it around.
places orders liquidate_position() Closes one position in this instrument completely.
places orders liquidate_all_positions() Closes every position this instrument holds, under every product.

Holdings

Holdings are shares kept for the long term in a demat account. Only Equity, FixedIncome, ExchangeTradedFund, InvestmentTrust and MutualFund carry these six members, and their orders are always sent under the cnc product.

Kind Member Description
active binding holdings The long-term holding of this share, merged across every broker.
active binding holdings_value What the shares held are worth at the moment.
active binding holdings_pnl What the shares held have made or lost.
places orders add_to_holdings() Buys more of this share to keep.
places orders reduce_holdings() Sells some of the shares held, without selling more than are free.
places orders liquidate_holdings() Sells every share held that is free to sell.

The account

Account acts on the whole account rather than on one instrument. It holds the kill switch and two readers of UBI’s order engine.

Kind Member Description
places orders flatten() Stops every synthetic order, cancels every open order at every broker, then closes every position in the account.
active binding parents Every synthetic order and held order the order engine has not finished, in every instrument.
method intent() Reads what the order engine did with one order after its placement stopped waiting.

Asset baskets

An asset basket is a group of instruments that is priced, analysed and stored as one, such as a portfolio, a watchlist or what an index or a fund holds. The Asset baskets page documents the classes below, each with its own members; two of Portfolio’s members place real orders.

Kind Member Description
class AssetBasket The shared base: live prices for every member in one request, weights, correlation, risk, and every analysis method.
class Portfolio What you hold, with a quantity per member: its value, its profit and loss, and orders for the whole basket.
places orders Portfolio$place_orders() Sends one market order per member, all in one request.
places orders Portfolio$rebalance() Sends the buys and sells that give the portfolio another basket’s weights.
class Watchlist Instruments followed together, each counting equally.
class Index A weighted index, published or your own, which can be turned into a portfolio.
class ExchangeTradedFundConstituents What an exchange traded fund holds, compared with the fund’s own price.
class MutualFundConstituents What a mutual fund holds, the only way to measure one.
class BasketStore, BasketCsvImporter Save and load baskets in MongoDB, and fill them from a CSV file.

The UBI client

UnifiedBrokerInterface is the HTTP client every instrument shares. You rarely call it directly, but it is how you reach a UBI route the package does not wrap. Unlike the Python client, its $new() also takes a credentials argument, a named list with api_key and api_secret that is used instead of reading them from MongoDB.

Kind Member Description
method connect() Exchanges the api key and secret for a new access token.
method disconnect() Revokes the access token in force on the server.
method status() Reports whether the session is connected and when its token expires.
method get() Sends a GET request.
method post() Sends a POST request.
method put() Sends a PUT request.
method patch() Sends a PATCH request.
method delete() Sends a DELETE request.

Reference pages

Two pages support all the others. Vocabulary lists every plain string the package passes through, such as "buy", "limit" and "cnc", in the style of Kite’s glossary of constants. Errors lists every error condition, which HTTP status from UBI signals it, and what to do next.
